items.headline: UK pledges hundreds of millions for AI safety and biosecurity
items.summary: The UK government announced fresh investment worth hundreds of millions of pounds in AI safety and security, including a new AI Biosecurity Lab and a King's Cross headquarters for the London Initiative for Safe AI. The funding targets threats ranging from cyber-attacks to advanced systems acting beyond human control.

items.headline: South Korea education minister resigns over AI cheating rules
items.summary: Education minister Choi Kyo-jin stepped down after last-minute measures to prevent AI cheating during the country's college entrance exam sparked public backlash. The rules, including phone alerts and eyeglass inspections, were announced just two days before more than half a million students sat the exam.

items.headline: AI agents autonomously conduct science in large experiment
items.summary: Over 12 weeks, 936 AI agents run by 35 human-led labs exchanged 9,500 messages across 229 chat rooms and published 936 studies. The experiment offers an eye-opening look at how autonomous agents might reshape scientific research.

items.headline: Writers push back on accusations of sounding like AI
items.summary: Nairobi writer Marcus Olang' faced accusations of writing like ChatGPT, prompting a broader debate about what it means to write 'like a human.' The piece critiques the rise of AI-detection paranoia and its colonial undertones.

items.headline: Families prepare for AI-driven 'vulnerability tsunami'
items.summary: As an Anthropic security executive warns of a coming 'vulnerability tsunami,' the NYT explores personal preparedness for AI-related disruptions. The piece reflects rising anxiety about AI risk entering mainstream consciousness.

items.headline: AI microdrama startup sells AI versions of actors' faces
items.summary: A startup is building a business around licensing AI likenesses of actors for microdramas, which VCs favor for their automation-driven growth stories. Industry figures remain skeptical about whether real audience demand exists for the AI content.

items.headline: Nature webinar examines AI's impact on science careers
items.summary: Nature Careers highlights growing concern that AI automation of coding and basic scientific tasks is threatening entry-level science jobs. A free webinar will discuss how researchers' roles, skills and job security are changing.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO raises record $107 billion
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, selling over 980 million shares for $81.3 billion plus $26 billion in a private placement, topping SpaceX's record. The maker of Claude navigated market jitters and regulatory fears as revenue surged to $33 billion in the first nine months of 2026.

items.headline: Anthropic lays out four ways it wants to disrupt science
items.summary: Following its IPO, Anthropic detailed ambitions to cure diseases, accelerate discovery and automate science. Many researchers remain skeptical of the firm's lofty claims.

items.headline: Google introduces Gemini 4 Neon model
items.summary: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Neon, bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across software engineering, knowledge work and science workflows. It follows the Gemini 4 Carbon release earlier in the month.

items.headline: The Economist calls 2027 'crunch time' for AI
items.summary: The Economist argues the coming year will be decisive for AI, after 2026 saw models solve hard math problems, run amok online and help target strikes in Iran. Debates over keeping AI under human control are intensifying.

items.headline: Enterprises still await AI's 'transformer moment'
items.summary: McKinsey's 2026 survey found 80% of respondents reported improved personal productivity but only 37% saw a positive contribution to enterprise EBIT. The gap reveals that high performers are those redesigning workflows rather than inserting AI into existing ones.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model
items.summary: Google made its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, available to developers, enterprises, scientists and consumers. It touts higher-precision knowledge work, improved agentic coding and state-of-the-art cybersecurity capabilities.

items.headline: Anthropic upgrades Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic released upgraded Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models with improvements in coding, reasoning and vision. In testing they completed complex software migrations, designed electronic devices and formalized a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours.
